summary.ja: VR で動作。3k プリセットで 60 fps（M1 Max）。ヘッドセットでレベルをまたいでプレイ済み
summary.en: Works in VR. 60 fps with the 3k preset (M1 Max); played in the headset across level changes

menu@3k.source: 2026-10-14, 58.8 and 54.1 fps after the geometry path fix (runs 20261014T074457Z, 20261014T074703Z); 18-21 before

known_issues.summary: Native ARM64: user reports magenta startup eyes and shadows breaking when their casters leave the headset view (session F9D54CC7-A0FC-4887-8F39-1979DF9A7485). Entirely magenta startup clears now present as black. Unsupported EDS3 dynamic colour masks select static variants before device creation. Native profiling also found frame workers serializing completed shader caches during head turns; completed asynchronous shaders now stay in the persistent worker archive, keeping engine exports small. Archive-mode workers no longer read or publish engine caches and never acquire their lock; unchanged exports reuse a real snapshot, invalidated by engine mutations with coherent size/data pairs. Progressive colour/depth draws remain nonblocking. Native checks/sanitizers and MoltenVK cache/depth-readback checks pass; isolated native probes and a control that restores cache publication reproduce and exercise the changed path. Final packaged-host/native-library probe records a 49 ms maximum sampled gap after second 30 and no gaps over 100 ms in that window (20261029T094446Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance o5-o6). The specific offscreen-caster flicker and headset gameplay still need a user retest; cold omitted draws can leave incomplete cached shadows until redrawn. No baseline or playtest level changed. Latest user headset retest confirms no freezes; alternating shadow presence remains unresolved, documented by two attached frames.
Saves made before 2026-10-14 (commit 8d10cfb) hold no level state: start the chapter again

notes: Needs -vr (scripts/launch_vxrt_alyx.sh passes it); without it the game starts in desktop mode.
2026-10-14: played in the headset at 3k through a2_quarantine_entrance -> a2_pistol (the level change that crashed before 8d10cfb); saves 2.5-6.2 MB.

2026-10-17: fences, foliage, fog and bottles that lit in one strong colour (red, green or blue) for single frames were reads beyond a constant buffer smaller than the shader declares (shader a10a2d66: cb3 37 float4s, 1 bound), fixed in 89e32a8; played on the MacBook Air without them, VXRT_FLASH_CAPTURE caught none in the game (before: 7 in about 90 s in the same rooms).

2026-10-19 (the user, in the Vision Pro's ALVR app with Joy-Con; not a harness run): the hands no longer vanish when ZL/ZR are left alone (ae75c23). Known: the buttons that pull the pistol's magazine out and reload are not where the game's controls put them (offset), but they work. The cause is not looked into (the ALVR client's Joy-Con mapping or this bridge's button mapping).

2026-10-23 (scratch run, not a harness run): with -novr -vulkan the game's Vulkan renderer (rendersystemvulkan.dll) runs on VXRuntime's own Vulkan (src/vk_*.m) flat on the Mac's screen: the main menu scene renders correctly (fog, lighting, textures, logo), 78-113 presents/s at 1512x982 on the M1 Max, 100 s without errors. Geometry shaders (vr_wireframe_hologram) are not supported there yet: those pipelines fail and the game goes on without them. Of Alyx's 14,898 Vulkan SPIR-V shaders (shaders_vulkan_000.vpk, read in a scratch directory), 14,843 translate and compile; 48 use function calls, 5 are geometry and 2 tessellation shaders.

2026-10-27: NativeARM has static ALVR integration for Pico 4 Ultra (session negotiation/restarts, IPD, per-hand actions and haptics, fenced stereo readback), covered by offline tests in NativeARM/tests. No Steam/game/headset run was performed for these changes; native picture, controls, audio, performance and playability remain unverified. The works/playable status and existing baselines in this profile refer to VXRuntime only. See NativeARM/README.md.

2026-10-27 (user session 0E9CB32E-60FB-4A51-94C2-C953794685A5, not a harness run): Pico 4 Ultra had a grey picture and pause sounds. Native logs show the start prompt and a paused game while frames keep being published/received. The missing stereo loading prompt and OpenVR binding-completion notifications are implemented, with raw trigger/action/frame diagnostics and offline tests. Their effect on menu entry and level changes has not been verified in the game. See NativeARM/README.md.

2026-10-27 (user session 9AE23E18-3FE0-48C9-B1B4-766C11F9C829, not a harness run): the loading prompt appears and trigger presses reach native shared memory, but UpdateActionState rejects the registered /user/gamepad restriction and hand actions remain inactive. Registered unbound sources and secondary-set complements are now supported, with an offline regression that failed before the fix and passes after it. Menu entry and native gameplay performance remain unverified; the paused black-frame session is not a gameplay benchmark.

2026-10-27 (user session 4761641F-E926-4FA5-AA66-37AD62EC5A37, not a harness run): the user reports native menu entry and normal frame rate. Remaining reports: sound on the Mac, waiting-for-headset UI during streaming, frozen picture after an in-game graphics preset change. The runtime keeps running but rejects Submit bounds. Uncached log timestamps, unique ALVR audio devices with no competing UDP capture, fixed Source 2 fidelity and detailed bounds diagnostics are implemented and covered where possible by offline tests. Audio and live preset changes need user verification; native playability is not established.

2026-10-27 (user session 85F7DE13-9D9F-48F4-B98F-FC44C0D76497, not a harness run): the user reports successful Pico 4 Ultra gameplay with good frame rate, but abrupt picture shifts and dropped held objects. A read-only shared-frame probe observed 8 zero pose timestamps in 865 frames over 12 seconds. A regression reproduced the interrupted pose-write path clearing hand input and the frame timestamp. Native sampling now reuses its last coherent packet without extending the 500 ms stale-input timeout; encoder frustum I/O moved outside pose publication. Offline runtime, syntax, encoder and sanitizer checks pass; the effect on headset symptoms remains unverified.

2026-10-27 (user report, not a harness run): Continuous movement does not walk and face buttons appear to turn the world camera with snap turning disabled. Session CAFDC9DC-9B0C-42DA-AA52-2DEB32F8DC8C shows stick deflection with Walk off. The runtime ignored the binding's force_input=position, analog deadzone/maxzone and D-pad sub_mode. These are now handled and covered by offline locomotion regressions; native normal/syntax/ASan/UBSan/TSan checks pass. Face-button turn commands are not present in the installed Touch bindings; transition diagnostics were added to establish the remaining symptom on the user's next run. No Valve files or user game settings were changed; headset verification is pending.

2026-10-27 (user session 4DFC0C08-3ADF-4E98-A1CE-7A506A056E37, not a harness run): A/X still turn the world while A also ejects the magazine. New logs show face presses with centred sticks and turning actions off. The runtime also exposed raw legacy controller state after loading the action manifest; read-only inspection of ARM64 libvr.so confirms a GetControllerState consumer. The runtime now makes action input exclusive, clears unavailable legacy states/poses, preserves modern magazine eject and keeps raw legacy input available before action selection. A regression failed before the fix; native normal/syntax/sanitizer checks pass. The user subsequently retested the latest app on Pico 4 Ultra and reports that everything works well; this confirms the accumulated fixes from the user's perspective without changing formal playtest levels or measured baselines.

2026-10-28 (native ARM user-log diagnosis and offline checks, not a harness run): session B5160DC2-54E3-49A5-A165-5A46AEE092EE sends the trigger hint before the engine pause and starts engine pipeline caches empty. Native loading now waits for the pause before displaying the trigger hint, suppresses the initial startup room/map, and renders the game-requested diorama with its transform and original pose timestamp. All colour/depth/stencil draws are retained; a persistent worker shader archive outside game files reuses completed shaders across empty engine caches and sessions without serializing on the drawing thread. Native regressions and sanitizers pass; synthetic MoltenVK tests verify warm archive reuse with empty/null caches and the first depth draw. First-ever shader compilation can still stall; live head-turn/shooting latency, shadow flicker and train-transition alignment remain unverified. A read-only render of the installed train diorama also reproduced its 85 MiB DDS being rejected by a 64 MiB limit and an inverted texture atlas; bounded mip upload and OBJ/DDS V-axis conversion correct those defects, with a sparse large-DDS regression and visual inspection. No performance baseline or playtest level changed.

2026-10-29 (native ARM user session E40B506D-A958-4B41-8AE0-11664FA46B6B and offline regression, not a harness run): the user confirms the trigger hint timing, but reports cold head-turn/pistol hitches and continuing shadow flicker. The all-first-draw-waits build logged roughly 250-590 ms bind waits and no failed/suppressed draws; retaining every draw did not resolve reported flicker. At the user's explicit preference for continuous rendering even with temporary holes, pending graphics binds now return immediately for colour and depth/stencil passes, omitting draws until the next stereo frame after compilation. Atomic demand priority and separate cache/queue locks prevent background compilation and cache work from blocking binds or enqueueing new materials. The persistent shader archive remains. A blocked-compiler regression fails before the change and passes after it; native checks, sanitizers and synthetic MoltenVK archive/depth-readback checks pass. Compute/unsupported graphics creation still has a synchronous fallback. Headset latency remains unverified and shadow flicker unresolved; progressive omission can leave incomplete cached shadows until redrawn. No gameplay baseline or playtest level changed.

2026-10-29 (native pink-frame user report, sessions 387E1E14-A5C3-4FFD-8A5F-F1C93DFD9475 and 5EEA16EB-AD6A-4A7E-878F-69D462F57DAC, not a harness run): both logs publish flat eye images before encoding and show no completed pipeline/archive import. A read-only synthetic import of the 12,960,564-byte persistent cache took 63,368.6 ms; a process sample found MoltenVK rebuilding Metal libraries during cache import. That import held the archive mutex on a material worker, starving all material workers while progressive drawing omitted every pending draw. Restoration now uses a dedicated thread and private cache; material workers skip busy archive operations and continue with current-session caches. The old file remains until import finishes; device teardown waits for the importer. The blocked-import regression fails before and passes after the change; native checks/sanitizers and MoltenVK cache/depth-readback checks pass. An optional GPU check completed a synthetic draw while restoring the user's cache through a private link, with the source SHA-256 unchanged; Metal was already warm from the first probe, so this is not a gameplay timing comparison. Headset confirmation and the separate shadow issue remain; no baseline or playtest level changed.

2026-10-29 (ARM startup/offscreen-caster report, offline regressions and isolated native probes): user session F9D54CC7-A0FC-4887-8F39-1979DF9A7485 starts with flat eye frames and requests VkPhysicalDeviceExtendedDynamicState3FeaturesEXT field #10, unsupported dynamic colour-write masks. Hiding EDS3 from this engine only on drivers without these masks selects static variants before vkCreateDevice; dynamic state on fully capable drivers is retained. Startup presentation replaces only entirely magenta clear eyes, in both eyes together, until scene content appears; later authored magenta survives. The startup regression fails before and passes after. Native checks, syntax, encoder checks, ASan/UBSan/TSan and the real MoltenVK capability/cache/depth-readback check pass. Native harness probes 20261029T084136Z-alyx-native-a1_intro_world_2 and 20261029T084312Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance complete without early exit or fatal diagnostics (o1, o7); control 20261029T084603Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance re-enables the incompatible extension and reproduces the unsupported device-feature request. These use private APFS overlays, simulated head turns and no encoder/headset, and are sealed in runs/ledger.jsonl. They do not prove the exact reported shadow flicker is gone or establish stall-free headset gameplay. The full VXRuntime check still fails on the previously documented translator differential cases; Windows sources were not changed. Existing gameplay baselines and playtest levels are unchanged. Packaged-host startup probe 20261029T085017Z-alyx-native-startup completes 65 seconds (o1), records zero sampled magenta-clear frames (o5), seven clear pairs presented as black (o16), no fatal diagnostics (o15) and no unsupported device-feature request (o17). Its largest sampled publication gap is 194 ms (o4); this is not a claim of hitch-free gameplay.

2026-10-29 (native head-turn cache profiling and regression): clean probe 20261029T085608Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance still records a 351 ms sampled publication gap (o4), after snapshot conversion was moved off the live sampler. Probe 20261029T085825Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance retains CPU stacks (o22) showing frame workers waiting for the cache mutex and serializing MoltenVK caches through klvk_GetPipelineCacheData. With the native default KL_VK_PRIVATE_CACHE=1 and a persistent archive configured, completed asynchronous shaders stay in the worker archive rather than growing engine caches exported during frames. Driver cache data remains real; unconfigured archive use retains the old policy. A deliberately blocked engine-publication regression fails before and passes after; native checks/sanitizers pass and real MoltenVK verifies unchanged engine-cache size, persistent shader reuse with empty/null caches and depth readback. Control 20261029T090907Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance disables the policy and reproduces a 665 ms sampled gap after second 30 (o5), two gaps over 100 ms (o6) and slow exports (o23). Private-cache probe 20261029T090344Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance has a 140 ms maximum including startup (o4). These are isolated simulated native diagnostics, not a new headset performance baseline; the particular offscreen shadow flicker still requires a user retest. Intermediate packaged probe 20261029T091427Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance still logs four slow 36-byte exports (o23), revealing remaining lock contention. Worker cache creation now runs outside the engine lock; unchanged private-archive snapshots are reused and invalidated on engine merges/inline creation while preserving a previously queried size/data pair. A regression fails before the reuse fix and passes after; export progress under blocked worker cache allocation and mutation coherence are covered by normal/sanitizer tests. Final archive-mode workers use only their archive, avoiding engine-cache seeding as well as publication; a blocked engine-seed regression fails before and passes after, with native/syntax/sanitizer/GPU checks passing. Final probe 20261029T093437Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance uses the verified host SHA-256 and records a 37 ms maximum sampled gap after second 30 (o5), no gaps over 100 ms in that window (o6), zero sampled magenta clears (o7), no fatal diagnostics (o20) and no unsupported device-feature errors (o22). Startup still includes a 126 ms sampled gap (o4) and slow cache operations (o23); this is not a claim of universally hitch-free gameplay. The offscreen-caster shadow symptom requires a headset retest. The delivered app host and its own MoltenVK are tested by 20261029T094446Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance: after second 30, maximum sampled gap 49 ms (o5), no gaps over 100 ms (o6), no sampled magenta clears (o7), no fatal diagnostics (o20) or unsupported feature errors (o22). Startup includes a 117 ms gap (o4). The nested host SHA-256 is verified unchanged after packaging; headset confirmation of the offscreen shadow symptom remains pending.

2026-10-29 (user headset follow-up, not a formal playtest or harness measurement): the user confirms that freezes are gone after the native shader-cache changes. Shadow flicker remains: attached successive views show a shadow absent, present, then absent again while its caster is outside the view. This supersedes any expectation that the EDS3 compatibility workaround alone fixed the shadow symptom. No formal playtest level or baseline changed.

2026-10-29 (later user follow-up, not a formal playtest): the user reports that shadow flicker stopped during the session and the current native build looks correct. No additional rendering fix was applied during this investigation, so its cause remains unproven. Native probe 20261029T102933Z-alyx-native-a2_quarantine_entrance verifies private save loading (s0/quick actually loads a1_intro_world_2), fixed-head burst capture (100 images, o22-o121), the requested duration (o1) and zero fatal diagnostics (o18). That viewpoint differs from the reported stairway and does not establish a shadow fix. Added bounded depth-attachment tracing is disabled by default. No gameplay baseline or playtest level changed.
